dimensions.name: Knowledge Delta
dimensions.justification: Adds several novel expert heuristics (usable‑memory calculator, shard‑count estimator, failover latency, immutable‑configuration table) that a baseline model would not know. Some sections merely restate AWS docs (e.g., basic encryption flags), preventing a perfect score.

dimensions.name: Mindset + Appropriate Procedures
dimensions.justification: Provides an AWS‑specific provisioning workflow (subnet‑group → parameter‑group → auth token → replication‑group) and decision trees that reflect real CloudOps reasoning. A few steps are generic (e.g., “verify prerequisites”) without AWS‑specific checks, costing one point.

dimensions.name: Anti-Pattern Quality
dimensions.justification: Extensive NEVER list with concrete reasons (e.g., AUTH without TLS, single‑AZ subnet for Multi‑AZ, using noeviction for a cache). Missing a few common pitfalls such as forgetting cost‑allocation tags, so not a full 15.

dimensions.name: Specification Compliance
dimensions.justification: Complete front‑matter, clear description, activation keywords, strict invocation contract, and exact output format with required labels. All required metadata present and well‑formed.

dimensions.name: Progressive Disclosure
dimensions.justification: Good layering: quick‑navigation table, high‑level mindset, then deep heuristics and procedures. However, the initial large tables and heuristics can overload the reader before the core checklist, reducing clarity.

dimensions.name: Freedom Calibration
dimensions.justification: Destructive actions (cluster creation) are tightly constrained: required engine choice, subnet‑group span, encryption flags, etc. Serverless section leaves many optional flags open, slightly under‑constraining a fragile operation.

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.justification: Follows a coherent pattern (Mindset → Navigation → Reasoning → Heuristics → Procedure → NEVER → Output). Minor inconsistency in section markers (mix of § and plain headings) prevents a perfect score.

dimensions.name: Practical Usability
dimensions.justification: Model output shows correct checklist and provisioning commands for Redis cases. However, the Memcached example uses ‘N/A’ values that do not match the defined output format (which expects ENABLED/DISABLED only), and the response includes multiple checklists in a single reply, violating the ‘first lines only’ contract. No example of PREREQUISITES_MISSING is shown.
